extra.message: POST /export/renewals/convert passes the request's format directly into an execSync shell command. Shell metacharacters in format execute arbitrary commands with the backend process's privileges. Any authenticated user can reach this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: POST /export/renewals/snapshot supplies label to path.join without containment validation. A label containing ../ escapes report-snapshots, allowing any authenticated user to create or overwrite writable .csv files elsewhere with the renewal report.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: POST /documents/import-from-source passes the x-document-source-url header directly to fetch. No destination restrictions prevent authenticated users from issuing backend requests to loopback, private-network services, or cloud metadata endpoints. Successful response bodies are stored as documents.

The external import buffers the entire attacker-selected HTTP response and writes it to disk without a size limit. An authenticated user can supply a server returning a very large response to exhaust backend memory or storage. The multipart upload's 50 MB limit does not apply here.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: GET /documents/:id/continue-workflow sends x-workflow-return-url directly to res.redirect. A caller controlling this header can make the endpoint redirect to an arbitrary external origin because no destination allowlist or same-origin check exists.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: When JWT_SECRET is absent, signing and verification use the public constant dev-secret-key-change-in-production, including in production mode. An attacker can forge a token whose sub identifies an existing privileged user; JwtStrategy obtains that user's permissions from the database.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Public registration accepts organizationId and immediately saves it as the new user's membership without validating an invitation or organization approval. Anyone knowing an organization's ID can register into it and receive a JWT granting customer access to its records.

Password-reset credentials are generated with Math.random, a non-cryptographic PRNG. The resulting value is the sole credential accepted by completePasswordReset, so account recovery depends on randomness that is unsuitable for security tokens.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: Successful password reset assigns undefined to the reset code and expiry before saving. TypeORM skips undefined properties, leaving both database values intact. The same token can therefore reset the password repeatedly until its original expiry. See [TypeORM save semantics](https://typeorm.io/docs/working-with-entity-manager/repository-api/).

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: GET /users/:id restricts account managers but performs no ownership check for customer contacts or support agents. These users can retrieve any known user's complete record, including passwordHash and active passwordResetCode, enabling cross-account disclosure and password-reset takeover.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: User.passwordResetCode, passwordResetExpiresAt, and passwordHash are selected and serialized without exclusion. Customer-accessible document, deal, escalation, comment, API-key, and webhook responses load complete related User entities. Customers can obtain staff password hashes and active recovery tokens even when accessing their own organization's records.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The global interceptor stores the first 500 characters of every successful non-GET response without redaction. Login and registration responses begin with access_token, causing bearer credentials to be persisted in audit_logs. User-update responses can also log password hashes and recovery data.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Every API-key creation logs issuedKey: rawKey alongside the organization and issuing user. This exposes the complete secret to application-log readers and log aggregation systems despite storing the database key as a bcrypt hash.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Billing synchronization sends BILLING_PROVIDER_API_KEY and organization billing context over HTTP. A network observer can recover the credential, and an intermediary can modify the request or response. Placing the credential in the query string additionally exposes it to URL logging.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: PATCH /organizations/:id calls update without the current user. The service loads solely by ID and saves supplied fields without assertOrganizationAccess. Any authenticated customer can change another organization's name, renewal date, billing contact, or notes and receive its record.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: PATCH /organizations/:id/status updates the organization without checking ownership or an authorized role. currentUser is used only for subsequent logging. Any authenticated user can suspend, cancel, or reactivate another organization's record by ID.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /organizations/:id loads all documents, escalations, deals, users, API keys, and webhooks and returns them through ...org. Customer membership is checked, but related records are not filtered. Customers receive internal and billing-only document metadata, internal escalation notes, and integration credential hashes that narrower endpoints restrict.

GET /escalations/:id returns the escalation with every comment, including isInternal comments, after only an organization check. The isInternal=false filter in getComments is bypassed by this detail response. internalNotes is also returned by both detail and list endpoints to customer contacts.

POST /escalations/:id/goodwill-credit has no role restriction and supplies no current user. issueGoodwillCredit updates solely by ID, bypassing findOne's ownership checks. Any authenticated customer can set another tenant's goodwill credit and retrieve the escalation, including its internal notes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The draft-followup-reply endpoint treats a CREDIT_APPROVED amount in assistant output as authorization to change goodwillCreditAmount. assistant-client.ts echoes the submitted prompt, so a customerFollowUp containing CREDIT_APPROVED: 5000 deterministically reaches this match and applies the credit without staff approval.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: Renewal, health, and escalation export routes have no role restrictions and pass no user context. Their services query all organizations or escalations. Any authenticated customer can export other tenants' billing contacts, renewal data, internal account notes, and support information. The labeled renewal export has the same exposure.

POST /import/contacts accepts organizationId without a role or ownership check and passes no current user to the service. Any authenticated customer can import arbitrary contacts into another organization, bypassing the tenant check on ordinary contact creation.

Document upload saves the request's organizationId and visibility without verifying that the caller may write to that organization. Any authenticated customer can place documents, including customer-visible files, in another tenant's library. Both URL-import creation methods also omit organization authorization.

POST /api-keys trusts createApiKeyDto.organizationId without checking tenant membership, ownership, or role. Any authenticated user can create an active key record for another organization and receive its plaintext key, bypassing the restrictions implemented by findOne.

POST /webhooks persists the submitted organizationId, URL, and event subscriptions without verifying organization access or role. Any authenticated customer can create active webhook configurations in another tenant using an attacker-selected destination.

GET /contacts scopes customers but does not scope account managers to organizations they own. Managers can omit organizationId to retrieve every tenant's contact PII and invitation tokens, or select an unowned organization. This bypasses the owner check in findOne.

GET /documents applies no organization-owner restriction to account managers. Managers can list documents for all organizations, including internal and billing-only metadata and uploader records, although findOne rejects documents belonging to unowned organizations.

GET /api-keys leaves its filter empty for account managers, exposing all organizations' key hashes, metadata, and creator records despite findOne's ownership restriction. A customer account with no organizationId also falls through to the unrestricted query.

GET /webhooks does not restrict account managers to owned organizations, exposing every tenant's webhook destinations, secret hashes, event subscriptions, and creator records. Customer accounts lacking organizationId also receive the unrestricted list.

Contact creation checks organization membership only for customer contacts. An account manager can create contacts in any organization by supplying its ID, even though findOne denies the same manager access when organization.ownerId differs.

POST /deals checks organizationId only for customer contacts. Account managers can insert deals with arbitrary values, stages, and assignments into organizations outside their assigned accounts, bypassing the owner restrictions used by deal listing and detail access.

Escalation creation validates tenant membership only for customer contacts. Account managers can submit an unowned organizationId and create escalations, internal notes, and staff assignments there, despite being denied that organization's existing escalations by findOne.

Support agents fall through to an unrestricted escalation query unless they voluntarily supply organizationId. Neither this query nor findOne verifies assignment to the agent or their team. Support agents can read and modify other agents' escalations across all tenants.

Deal mutations enforce tenant membership but no staff role. Customer contacts can create, edit, delete, and transition their organization's deals, including changing financial values and assignments. The frontend restricts deal management navigation to platform admins and account managers, but the backend permits customer requests.

UpdateDealDto permits stage, and PATCH /deals/:id assigns it directly. An authorized caller can jump from lead to closed_won or perform other transitions rejected by /deals/:id/stage, bypassing ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS and corrupting the enforced pipeline workflow.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Document update and deletion reuse findOne's read-access check without checking uploader ownership or a staff role. A customer who can download a shared staff-uploaded document can also change its metadata or visibility and permanently delete both its file and database record.

API-key rotation checks only organization access, allowing customer contacts to rotate staff-created organization keys and obtain the replacement plaintext key. Revocation uses the same insufficient check. These privileged integration-management actions have no server-side role restriction.

Webhook mutation requires only findOne's organization check. Customer contacts can alter staff-created webhook URLs, secrets, event subscriptions, and activation state or delete the configurations. Backend role checks do not enforce the staff-only integration management shown by the frontend.

Escalation update permits customer contacts to overwrite internalNotes because only tenant membership is checked before Object.assign. Assignment likewise accepts any assignedToId without a staff-role check. Customers can manipulate internal support records and ownership instead of being limited to customer-visible updates and replies.

Customer-controlled escalation subjects are exported with csv-stringify without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. A subject such as =HYPERLINK(...) is interpreted as a formula when staff open the CSV. Organization names and notes reach the renewal and health exports through the same unprotected pattern.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: POST /contacts/:id/activity-notes interpolates the request's action and note directly into a log message. Neither field has newline or control-character neutralization. A caller with contact access can inject additional log lines and forge activity messages.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: The global exception filter replaces its generic message with exception.message for unexpected errors and returns that message to the caller. Request-triggered database, filesystem, and converter failures therefore expose internal schema details, paths, or command diagnostics in production responses.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Seeding creates enabled administrator, manager, support, and customer accounts with the shared hardcoded password password123. Any deployment retaining these demo accounts permits login with publicly documented credentials, including platform administrator access.

Public login performs password comparisons without failed-attempt tracking, throttling, or temporary lockout. No application-wide rate limiter is registered. An attacker can make unrestricted password guesses against known accounts; the public workspace handoff authentication routes also lack attempt limits.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: JWT validation checks only user existence and isActive. Password reset changes passwordHash without revoking tokens or updating a token version checked here. A stolen bearer token remains usable after the victim resets their password, until its original 24-hour expiration.

The public ticket-status endpoint returns 404 for a nonexistent ticket but 403 for an existing ticket belonging to another organization. An unauthenticated caller can distinguish valid ticket IDs without knowing their organization, leaking ticket existence.

Any authenticated user can supply a template rendered synchronously without execution or output limits. The controller also accepts recipientContactName without runtime type validation, allowing an array. Nested #each blocks repeatedly iterating that array can multiply output exponentially and exhaust CPU or memory. See [Handlebars iteration helpers](https://handlebarsjs.com/guide/builtin-helpers.html#each).
